items.title: Utility of Donor-Recipient HLA Matching in Heart Transplantation in the Era of Extended Donor Organ Preservation: A Multi-Institutional Analysis.
items.abstract: Closer human leukocyte antigen (HLA) match between the donor and the recipient leads to better outcomes after kidney transplantation. Since extended donor preservation is now possible in heart transplantation (HT), we examined the possible impact of prioritization of HLA matching in HT. We included single organ HT recipients reported to the Organ Procurement and Transplantation Network (OPTN) transplanted in 2010-2019. Outcomes included survival, treated rejection and development of cardiac allograft vasculopathy (CAV) across 5 and 10 year follow-up after transplant. We examined associations between matches at A, B, DR, DPB, DQA, DQB and DPA loci and the outcomes in univariable and multivariable analyses. There were 5176 patients in the 5Y cohort with a median of 9 (IQR 8; 11) HLA mismatches and 9118 patients in the 10Y cohort with a median of 6 (IQR 5; 7) HLA mismatches. In adjusted analyses, there was no significant association between donor-recipient HLA match and mortality, treated rejection or CAV in the 5Y cohort. In the 10Y cohort, HLA mismatch was a risk factor for mortality (HR 1.06, CI 1; 1.12, p=0.047) and treated rejection (HR 1.13, CI 1.07;1.2, p<0.001) in adults. Among pediatric patients, HLA mismatch conferred a nominally higher risk of mortality (HR 1.14, CI 0.97; 1.34, p=0.121) and treated rejection (HR 1.08, CI 0.96;1.21, p=0.226). We show that the current impact of donor-recipient HLA match on post-HT outcomes is relatively small. While novel organ preservation techniques may make HLA matching feasible, our data do not support its adoption into future iterations of the HT allocation system.

items.title: Carotid and femoral plaque burden in patients with early coronary artery disease events: Prevalence, extent and relationship to risk phenotypes.
items.abstract: Early coronary artery disease events (eCAD) are increasing, occasionally occurring in individuals with minimal atherosclerosis, suggesting heterogeneous underlying mechanisms. We report, for the first time, carotid and femoral plaque burden in eCAD patients, relate it to underlying phenotypes, and compare it with the PESA reference cohort to explore preventive implications. eCAD patients (<60 years) were consecutively and prospectively enrolled at a tertiary hospital. Conventional and non-conventional cardiovascular risk factors (CVRF) and blood biomarkers were assessed, and global atherosclerosis plaque burden (GPB) was quantified as total carotid and femoral plaque volume by 3-dimensional vascular ultrasound (3DVUS). Among 231 eCAD patients (53 ± 5 years old; 14% women; 23% with a prior event; 52% presented with STEMI) conventional CVRF were frequent but prevalence of non-conventional CVRF was high (28% elevated lipoprotein a, 25% family history of eCAD, 25% hyperuricemia, and 14% hyperhomocysteinemia). Underlying GPB was high (268.7 mm3 [IQR75.2-509.9]), being higher in the femoral than the carotid territory (200.6 mm3 [IQR51.7-420.7] vs 35.2 mm3 [IQR7.9-96.2], p < 0.001), and increased with age. Compared with age-matched asymptomatic individuals (PESA study), eCAD patients had markedly higher GPB (284.1 mm3 [IQR110-546.8] vs 50.8 mm3 [18.7-121.5]). However, GPB in eCAD patients varied widely. Severe GBP (percentile≥75th) identified a subgroup with predominantly conventional CVRF and prior CAD, with marginal presence of non-conventional factors, compared with those with no-or-mild GPB (percentile≤25th). Carotid and femoral PB by 3DVUS identifies distinct pathophysiological phenotypes in eCAD, underscoring the value of atherosclerosis assessment for individualized management and prevention.

items.title: Mycobacterium bovis Cardiac Implantable Electronic Device Infection Following Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin Therapy.
items.abstract: Intravesical Bacillus Calmette-Guérin (BCG) is an established treatment for non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer. Although disseminated Mycobacterium bovis BCG infection is a recognized complication of BCG therapy, cardiac implantable electronic device (CIED) involvement is exceptionally rare. We report the second published case of BCG-related CIED infection. A 66-year-old man with an implantable cardioverter-defibrillator (ICD) presented with persistent fever following intravesical BCG therapy. Despite appropriate treatment of concomitant Serratia marcescens bacteremia, fever persisted. Echocardiography was non-diagnostic, whereas 18F-FDG PET/CT suggested device infection. Following complete device and lead extraction, polymerase chain reaction (PCR) of explanted material identified Mycobacterium tuberculosis complex, and cultures subsequently confirmed M. bovis BCG. Concurrent pulmonary involvement was microbiologically confirmed, and the clinical course was further complicated by immune thrombocytopenia. Antimycobacterial therapy resulted in clinical and radiological improvement, and a subcutaneous ICD was successfully implanted after infection control. BCG-related CIED infection should be considered in patients with persistent fever following intravesical BCG therapy, even when echocardiography is non-diagnostic. PET/CT and PCR of explanted device material may facilitate earlier diagnosis and guide management.

items.title: Immune landscape and immunotherapeutic strategies for the treatment of TP53-mutated acute myeloid leukemia.
items.abstract: TP53-mutated acute myeloid leukemia (AML) represents the treatment-refractory subtype of AML, characterized by high relapse rates and poor clinical outcomes. Despite advancements in AML treatment with currently approved agents and allogeneic hematopoietic cell transplantation, overall survival for patients with TP53-mutated AML remains dismal, underscoring the urgent need for innovative therapeutic strategies. TP53 mutations contribute to treatment resistance by impairing apoptosis and fostering immune evasion through mechanisms such as regulatory immune cell expansion, immune checkpoint overexpression, and dysregulation of the bone marrow microenvironment. Immunotherapy has emerged as an area of active investigation to overcome therapeutic resistance and improve clinical outcomes. While TP53-specific clinical data are currently available for only a limited number of immunotherapeutic approaches, several emerging modalities have demonstrated biological or clinical activity in AML more broadly and possess a strong biological rationale for investigation in TP53-mutated disease based on the unique immune landscape of this molecular subtype. This review summarizes the immune mechanisms of treatment resistance in TP53-mutated AML, provides an overview of the current landscape of immunotherapy, and discusses future directions, including rational combination strategies, patient selection, and optimized therapeutic timing to achieve durable responses and improve survival in this high-risk population.

items.title: Immunomodulatory therapies in bacterial community-acquired pneumonia: Current evidence and future directions.
items.abstract: Community-acquired pneumonia remains a leading cause of morbidity and mortality worldwide, accounting for more than two million deaths annually. While most patients successfully clear pulmonary infection through an effective host immune response, a subset progress to severe disease characterised by dysregulated and excessive inflammation. This maladaptive immune response drives subsequent organ dysfunction and mortality, prompting increasing interest in immunomodulatory therapies as adjunctive treatments. This article aims to describe the key immunomodulatory strategies investigated for the management of bacterial community-acquired pneumonia, summarise the evidence for their efficacy and limitations, and highlight potential future therapeutic approaches. We conducted a comprehensive literature search of Medline, Embase, Web of Science, Scopus and Global Health, using search terms related to pneumonia and immunomodulatory intervention from database inception to December 8 th , 2025. While a broad range of immunomodulatory strategies has been investigated in bacterial community-acquired pneumonia, few have been shown to be reliably beneficial. Corticosteroids are the most extensively studied agents and have been associated with clinically relevant outcomes in selected patient populations, supporting guideline recommendations for their use in severe community-acquired pneumonia. Targeted inhibition of inflammatory cytokines and downstream signalling pathways has been explored to a lesser degree, with limited evidence supporting its use in bacterial community-acquired pneumonia. Other approaches, including passive immunotherapy and immune stimulation, have been investigated, but current evidence supporting their routine use remains inconclusive. Immunomodulation represents an important adjunctive therapeutic strategy in bacterial community-acquired pneumonia. Although progress has been made, particularly with corticosteroids, evidence remains incomplete. Further high-quality research is required to better define patient selection, optimal timing, and the clinical impact of immunomodulatory therapies.

items.title: Single-cell profiling reveals systemic immune reprogramming in muscle-invasive urothelial carcinoma.
items.abstract: Urothelial carcinoma progression to muscle-invasive disease involves poorly understood systemic immune alterations. We performed single-cell RNA sequencing of peripheral blood mononuclear cells from 20 UC patients, analyzing 144,019 cells with public datasets. MIUC showed profound immune reprogramming: T/NK cells exhibited metabolic stress and suppression, while monocytes exhibited transcriptional features suggestive of pro-tumor reprogramming, potentially involving TGF-β signaling. Enhanced intercellular communication coordinated immunosuppression. These findings reveal stage-specific immune remodeling, providing a foundation for systemic immunotherapies in advanced UC.

items.title: Determinants of Systemic Anticancer Treatment and Continuous Intravenous Opioid and/or Benzodiazepine Use at End of life: A Real-World Analysis of Demographic and Clinical Factors in Advanced Cancer Patients.
items.abstract: Systemic-anticancer-treatment (SACT) near the end of life (EOL) remains common despite limited evidence of meaningful survival benefit and concerns regarding treatment-related toxicity and quality of life. Here, we aimed to identify demographic and clinical factors associated with SACT and continuous intravenous opioid and/or benzodiazepine use at EOL, with a specific focus on adolescent and young adult (AYA) patients. In this retrospective cohort study adult patients with cancer treated with palliative intent at the Medical University of Vienna between 2013 and 2021 were included. SACT at EOL was defined as systemic antineoplastic therapy administered ≤30 days before death. Continuous intravenous opioid and/or benzodiazepine use at EOL was defined as ongoing hydromorphone, morphine and/or midazolam administration via syringe pump at the time of death. Univariable and multivariable logistic regression analyses were performed. A predefined subgroup analysis examined AYA patients (<40 years). Among 775 patients (median age 65 years; 51% female), 358 (46%) SACT within 30 days before death. In multivariable analysis, younger age (OR 0.99 per year increase, 95% CI 0.98-1.00, p=0.043) and male sex (female vs male: OR 0.64, 95% CI 0.48-0.85, p=0.002) were independently associated with SACT at EOL. In a sensitivity analysis, AYA status was associated with higher odds of SACT (OR 2.32, 95% CI 1.32-4.23, p=0.004). Continuous intravenous opioid and/or benzodiazepine use at EOL was documented in 343 patients (44%); recent SACT was independently associated with higher odds of medication use (OR 4.93, 95% CI 3.63-6.74, p<0.001). Among 55 AYA patients (7.1%), SACT (65% vs 45%) and continuous intravenous opioid and/or benzodiazepine use (67% vs 43%) were more frequent than among non-AYA patients aged ≥40 years. SACT at EOL remains common and was independently associated with younger age and male sex. AYA patients also showed higher odds of SACT in a sensitivity analysis, although this finding should be interpreted cautiously given the small subgroup size. Higher rates of both interventions among AYA patients highlight the need for early, age- and sex-sensitive palliative care integration.

items.title: Infectious Disease Screening in Hematopoietic Cell Donors: Risk Assessment, Regulation, and Selective Donor Utilization.
items.abstract: Donor-derived infections in hematopoietic cell transplantation (HCT) are uncommon but potentially severe complications that remain largely preventable through rigorous donor screening and risk mitigation strategies. Although reported incidence appears low, donor-derived infections are associated with substantial morbidity and mortality when transmission occurs in profoundly immunocompromised recipients. In the United States, donor eligibility is governed by Food and Drug Administration requirements for screening and testing for relevant communicable disease agents and diseases. European and international frameworks similarly require comprehensive donor evaluation and testing for major transmissible infections, with additional testing guided by epidemiologic and exposure risk. A key challenge across jurisdictions is distinguishing regulatory donor eligibility from clinical donor suitability and determining when individualized donor-recipient risk assessment is appropriate. Advances in nucleic acid testing have markedly shortened diagnostic window periods for blood-borne pathogens. Concurrently, highly effective antiviral therapies, particularly for hepatitis B and hepatitis C, have transformed select historically prohibitive infections into increasingly manageable risks. These developments have supported selective clinical consideration of donors who remain ineligible under traditional regulatory criteria when an applicable regulatory pathway permits use. This review examines pathogen-specific transmission risk, contemporary screening strategies, and evolving approaches to donor eligibility in HCT. Future donor screening frameworks will likely evolve toward adaptive, pathogen-specific models that integrate molecular diagnostics, recipient mitigation strategies, and real-world transplant outcomes to optimize both safety and donor access.

items.title: Association of GLP-1 receptor agonist therapy with cardiovascular outcomes in patients with MASLD: A translational study.
items.abstract: Patients with metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) and type 2 diabetes (T2D) are at increased risk of adverse cardiovascular outcomes, potentially involving systemic metabolic dysfunction and cardiac remodeling. Glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists (GLP-1 RAs) improve metabolic dysfunction in MASLD; however, their associations with cardiovascular outcomes and effects on MASLD-associated cardiac remodeling remain incompletely understood. In this translational study, we integrated a real-world TriNetX cohort of patients with MASLD and T2D with complementary experimental studies in a mouse model of MASLD. Following propensity score matching, 42,910 patients were included in each treatment group. GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with a lower risk of the primary composite cardiovascular outcome compared with sulfonylurea therapy (hazard ratio 0.87, 95% confidence interval 0.84-0.91; P < 0.001), although this association was not statistically significant in 90-day and 180-day landmark analyses. In Western diet-fed mice, GLP-1 RA treatment improved selected indices of cardiac function and attenuated cardiomyocyte hypertrophy. Although myocardial fibrosis was numerically reduced, the difference compared with vehicle-treated mice was not statistically significant (P = 0.28). Molecular analyses showed reduced expression of fibrosis- and extracellular matrix remodeling-related markers, including CTGF, TGF-β1, and vimentin. Collectively, GLP-1 RA therapy was associated with lower cardiovascular risk in the primary observational analysis, although this finding was not consistently supported by sensitivity analyses. Complementary experimental findings suggest improvements in selected cardiac functional indices and changes in fibrosis-associated molecular remodeling, warranting further investigation.

items.title: Pneumococcal vaccine after hematopoietic cell transplantation: a rapid review of four-dose pneumococcal conjugate vaccine schedules.
items.abstract: Hematopoietic cell transplant (HCT) recipients are at substantially elevated risk for invasive pneumococcal disease (IPD) due to prolonged immunocompromised state, yet optimal pneumococcal vaccine product selection and scheduling, including the role of higher-valency pneumococcal conjugate vaccines (PCVs), have not undergone Advisory Committee on Immunization Practices review. We conducted a rapid review to synthesize evidence on the immunogenicity and safety of four-dose PCV schedules in HCT recipients to inform future clinical guidance. Following Cochrane rapid review methods and PRISMA guidelines, we searched Medline, Embase, and Scopus (initial: November 2024; updated: March 2025) and identified 31 eligible studies. Four studies directly evaluated four-dose PCV13 or PCV15 regimens in allogeneic HCT recipients, and only one study provided a direct randomized comparison. Among studies that allowed comparison, four-dose PCV13 schedules consistently generated higher overall and serotype-specific IgG and opsonophagocytic activity responses than three-dose PCV13 followed by 23-valent pneumococcal polysaccharide vaccine (PPSV23), while PPSV23 provided limited additional benefit when administered within 1-2 months of the final PCV13 dose. Both randomized and nonrandomized studies demonstrated robust antibody responses following the fourth PCV dose, and safety profiles were acceptable. Although adverse events were more frequent after the fourth PCV dose, serious vaccine-related events were rare and difficult to attribute given underlying comorbidities. Findings from 27 supporting studies further contextualized optimal timing and product choice, showing that later initiation (≥6 months post-HCT) was often associated with stronger and more durable immune responses, although waning immunity remained common. PCV-based regimens were consistently more immunogenic than PPSV23-only schedules. No studies evaluated PCV20 or PCV21 in HCT recipients, representing a major evidence gap despite their expanded serotype coverage. Overall, the available evidence provides evidence of immunogenicity and safety with a four-dose PCV-based schedule initiated 3-6 months post-HCT, while critical research gaps remain regarding higher-valency PCVs, mixed-product schedules, and strategies tailored to transplant type or individual immunologic risk.

items.title: Predictors of Incident Hepatic Fibrosis and Steatotic Liver Disease-Associated Fibrosis Among Women with and without HIV.
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis is an important cause of non-AIDS morbidity among women with HIV (WWH), but predictors of incident fibrosis in the absence of viral hepatitis are not well defined. We included women with and without HIV enrolled in the Women's Interagency HIV Study (WIHS), now part of the MACS/WIHS Combined Cohort Study, who underwent vibration-controlled transient elastography (VCTE) between 2013 and 2020 as part of the Liver Disease and Reproductive Aging (LIVRA) Study and had at least two VCTE exams. Participants with viral hepatitis, heavy alcohol use, or baseline fibrosis were excluded. Poisson regression estimated incidence rate ratios (IRRs) for incident fibrosis, defined as liver stiffness ≥7.1 kPa. Models included time-updated covariates and tested interactions between HIV and steatosis measured by controlled attenuation parameter (CAP). Among 1,036 women (709 WWH, 327 without HIV), median age was 49 years and median BMI 32 kg/m2. Over a mean follow-up of 3.5 years, 19% developed incident fibrosis. HIV infection (IRR 1.72, 95% CI 1.12-2.65) and higher CAP (per 10 dB/m; IRR 1.04, 95% CI 1.00-1.08) were associated with fibrosis in multivariable adjusted models. The association between CAP and fibrosis differed by HIV status (interaction p = 0.02) and was attenuated among WWH. Fibrosis without steatosis accounted for 28% of new fibrosis in WWH and was more common in those with prior AIDS. HIV infection predicted incident hepatic fibrosis, while steatosis was a weaker predictor in WWH. Fibrosis without steatosis was common, suggesting distinct fibrosis phenotypes and potential HIV-specific pathways of liver injury.

items.title: Burden, patterns, and challenges of HIV-associated malignancies in Nigeria: a narrative review.
items.abstract: Nigeria bears one of the world's largest burdens of HIV, with ongoing expansion of antiretroviral therapy (ART) significantly improving the survival of people living with HIV (PLHIV). This epidemiologic shift has changed the pattern of morbidity and mortality toward chronic conditions, especially HIV-associated malignancies (HIVAMs), including both AIDS-defining malignancies (ADMs) and non-AIDS-defining malignancies (NADMs). Despite their increasing significance, the national burden, patterns, and systemic challenges related to HIVAMs in Nigeria remain poorly understood and characterized. We conducted a narrative review of peer-reviewed literature, cancer registry reports, and grey literature published between January 2000 and December 2024. Searches were carried out in PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, African Journals Online, and Google Scholar, complemented by national reports from the National Agency for the Control of AIDS, the Federal Ministry of Health, and the National System of Cancer Registries. Eligible sources reported cancer occurrence among PLHIV or HIV prevalence among cancer patients in Nigeria. Findings were synthesized narratively due to significant heterogeneity across study designs and outcomes. Seventy-three sources met the inclusion criteria, and these were primarily hospital-based and retrospective studies. ADMs remain the most common cancers among PLHIV, notably invasive cervical cancer, Kaposi sarcoma, and non-Hodgkin lymphoma, with notable regional differences. Expansion of ART has been linked to a decline in Kaposi sarcoma incidence, while the burden of cervical cancer remains high, driven by persistent oncogenic HPV infection and limited screening coverage among women living with HIV (WLWH). Emerging NADMs, such as hepatocellular carcinoma, Hodgkin lymphoma, breast cancer, and ocular surface squamous neoplasia, reflect improved survival, aging, chronic immune dysregulation, and co-infections like Hepatitis B and C. Across these cancers, late-stage presentation and poor outcomes are common, largely due to fragmented HIV-cancer surveillance, inadequate pathology and radiotherapy capacity, limited molecular diagnostics, high out-of-pocket treatment costs, and weak integration of HIV and oncology services. HIV-associated cancers pose a major yet often overlooked public health issue in Nigeria. Enhancing integrated HIV-cancer surveillance, increasing prevention and early detection efforts through ART programs, upgrading diagnostic and treatment facilities, and utilizing digital and molecular innovations are essential for decreasing preventable cancer-related morbidity and mortality among PLHIV in Nigeria.

items.title: Ginsenoside Rh1 exerts hepatoprotective effects against liver fibrosis through induction of ferroptosis via SLC7A11 inhibition.
items.abstract: Liver fibrosis is a critical pathological stage in the progression from chronic liver disease to cirrhosis, and the exploration of preventive agents derived from traditional Chinese medicine offers considerable potential. However, the precise role and molecular mechanism of ginsenoside Rh1 (Rh1) in liver fibrosis remain largely obscure. This study investigated the anti-fibrotic mechanism of Rh1, focusing on ferroptosis. In vitro, Rh1 dose-dependently suppressed the viability of activated hepatic stellate cells (HSCs) and concurrently induced key ferroptosis features. In vivo, Rh1 administration markedly attenuated carbon tetrachloride-induced liver fibrosis, improved histological architecture, and restored liver function. Mechanistically, transcriptomic analysis and molecular validation identified SLC7A11, a core regulator of ferroptosis, as a binding partner of Rh1. Rescue experiments confirmed that the pro-ferroptotic and anti-fibrotic effects of Rh1 were functionally dependent on SLC7A11 inhibition. In conclusion, our findings demonstrated that ginsenoside Rh1 alleviated liver fibrosis by targeting SLC7A11 to promote the ferroptosis in cultured HSCs, unveiling a novel pharmacological mechanism. This work provided a compelling preclinical rationale for developing Rh1 as a promising preventive agent against liver fibrosis.

items.title: Metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease after pancreaticoduodenectomy: Mechanisms, clinical impact, and therapeutic implications.
items.abstract: Pancreaticoduodenectomy (PD) is associated with increasingly recognized long-term metabolic sequelae. Among these, metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease (MASLD) is emerging as a frequent but underappreciated phenomenon. Current evidence suggests that post-PD MASLD may represent a distinct metabolic phenotype driven predominantly by pancreatic exocrine and endocrine insufficiency, malnutrition, and altered gastrointestinal physiology rather than classical metabolic syndrome. These alterations may disrupt lipid metabolism, mitochondrial function, and hepatocellular homeostasis, promoting hepatic steatosis. Limited observational evidence has also associated post-PD MASLD with poorer survival, reduced chemotherapy tolerance, and challenges in postoperative imaging surveillance. Further characterization of its pathophysiology and clinical significance is needed to inform preventive and treatment strategies and optimize long-term outcomes. This review aims to summarize current evidence on the incidence, pathophysiology, clinical significance, and management of de novo MASLD following PD.

items.title: Bisphenol S facilitates breast cancer progression through DRP1-mediated mitophagy.
items.abstract: To investigate the pro‑metastatic effects of low-dose bisphenol S (BPS) and characterize the underlying molecular pathway in breast cancer (BC). HER2‑amplified MMTV‑Erbb2 mice received BPS‑laced drinking water (50 μg/L) to assess tumor growth and metastasis. BC cell migration, invasion, and proliferation were evaluated after BPS treatment. RNA‑seq and bioinformatics identified key pathways. PINK1 or DRP1 knockdown, together with pharmacological inhibition of DRP1 (Mdivi‑1), were employed to verify the role of mitophagy in vitro and in vivo. Clinical relevance was assessed via immunohistochemistry and public databases (TCGA, GEO). Environmentally relevant BPS exposure accelerated BC progression in mice, increasing primary tumor burden, lung/liver metastasis and an EMT‑like signature (upregulated FN, MMP‑2, Snail; downregulated E‑cadherin) with elevated oxidative stress. In vitro, BPS promoted migration and invasion without affecting proliferation in MCF-7 and BT474 cells. RNA‑seq revealed transcriptomic changes; KEGG enrichment identified mitophagy as a central pathway. BPS induced mitochondrial dysfunction (depolarization, ROS accumulation, ATP depletion) and activated PINK1/Parkin‑mediated mitophagy (increased MAP1LC3B-II, reduced P62/TOM20). Genetic knockdown of PINK1 or DRP1, as well as pharmacological inhibition of DRP1 by Mdivi‑1, reversed BPS‑induced mitophagy, restored mitochondrial homeostasis (mitochondrial length and membrane potential), and suppressed the pro‑migratory and pro‑invasive phenotypes. In vivo, Mdivi‑1 attenuated BPS‑driven tumor progression and metastasis. Clinically, elevated DRP1 and PINK1 in BC tissues correlated with lymph node metastasis, advanced TNM stage, and worse overall survival. Environmental‑level BPS exposure promotes BC metastasis via DRP1/PINK1‑dependent mitophagy. DRP1 and PINK1 are identified as potential prognostic biomarkers and therapeutic targets for reducing cancer risk from environmental carcinogens.

items.title: The potential impact of radiation-synthesized chitosan coated titanium dioxide nanoparticles on hepatocellular carcinoma: Modulation of autophagy via AMPK, mTOR, and ULK-1 pathways in a rat model.
items.abstract: Liver cancer remains a major clinical challenge due to limited treatment options and significant treatment-related toxicity. Nanotechnology offers new avenues to enhance therapeutic efficacy and tissue specificity while reducing systemic adverse effects. This study emphasizes the protective effect of chitosan-coated titanium dioxide nanoparticles (CS-TiO 2 NPs) against hepatocellular carcinoma (HCC) induced in rats. To evaluate whether CS-TiO 2 NPs can mitigate DEN-induced hepatocellular carcinoma in rats by modulating autophagy via AMPK, mTOR, and ULK-1 pathways, restoring redox balance, and suppressing tumor-promoting signaling. Adult rats were allocated to six groups, including normal controls, DEN-induced cancer controls, chitosan coated titanium dioxide nanoparticles controls, 5-Fluorouracil controls, CS-TiO2 NPs plus DEN treatment and 5-FU plus DEN. Biochemical assays assessed hepatic injury (ALT, AST), renal function (urea, creatinine), oxidative stress (MDA, GSH), and tumor markers (β-catenin, NOTCH1, AFP). Autophagy-related signaling (AMPK, ULK-1, mTOR), apoptosis was evaluated by measuring Annexin V and measuring of Cytochrome P450 2E1 (CYP2E1) for detecting drug metabolism, toxicology and overall biological response, complemented by histopathology to characterize liver architecture and tumor-associated changes. CS-TiO 2 NPs treatment significantly reduced DEN-induced hepatic injury, evidenced by significant decrease in ALT and in AST relative to cancer controls, and substantially improved renal function (urea and creatinine reduction). Redox balance was favorably shifted, with marked reductions in MDA and restoration of GSH, especially with γ-irradiation-synthesized CS-TiO 2 NPs. Oncogenic signaling was attenuated, with a meliorative decrease in β-catenin and NOTCH1 in the CS-TiO 2 NPs treated group compared with cancer controls. Autophagy-related markers indicated restoration of autophagic activity: DEN suppressed AMPK and ULK-1 and elevated mTOR, whereas CS-TiO 2 NPs reversed these alterations, suggesting reactivation of autophagy initiation signaling network. Apoptosis assessments revealed increased pro-death signaling in treated groups, aligning with enhanced tumor cell clearance. Histopathological evaluation demonstrated improved hepatic architecture and reduced tumor-associated pathology with CS-TiO 2 NPs treatment. CS-TiO 2 nanoparticles confer a dual protective effect in DEN-induced rat HCC by directly modulating tumor-promoting signaling and by re-programming autophagy and redox homeostasis to favor tumor suppression and hepatic integrity. The observed downregulation of β-catenin and NOTCH1, together with restored AMPK-ULK-1-mTOR signaling and improved histology, supports the potential of CS-TiO 2 NPs as multifunctional nanotherapeutics for liver cancer. Further work should elucidate precise autophagic flux dynamics, biodistribution, and long-term safety to facilitate clinical translation.
